speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if the pain is localized to one wrist or both?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Arthritis (Lyme Disease).

The combination of a recent Minnesota camping trip, a preceding self-resolving monoarthritis (likely Lyme arthritis at the knee), and new onset of fever, malaise, and wrist pain with chills is highly specific for disseminated Lyme disease. I will proceed with requesting images of the wrist to look for swelling or effusion and confirm the diagnosis via serology if available.
